claims.text: Mechanical alloying followed by short-duration annealing below the recrystallization temperature will produce a hierarchical microstructure with dense dislocation tangles and nanoscale solute clusters.
The proposed hierarchical microstructure will simultaneously improve room-temperature strength and ductility in brittle MPEAs.
The candidate starting alloy has a coarse-grained, single-phase FCC or BCC structure.
The starting alloy's brittleness arises from limited dislocation mobility and insufficient strain-hardening capacity.
High-energy ball milling for 20–40 hours will induce severe plastic deformation and solute segregation.
Spark plasma sintering 100–150 °C below the onset of recrystallization for 5–10 minutes will preserve the mechanically alloyed non-equilibrium structure.
Completing room-temperature tensile testing within 24 hours of sintering will prevent significant coarsening before testing.
The proposed treatment will produce ultrafine grains smaller than 1 µm with high dislocation density.
The proposed treatment will produce nanoscale, coherent, solute-rich clusters through non-equilibrium segregation during the short anneal.
The resulting microstructure will be dual-phase or spatially graded.
The solute-rich clusters will act as strengthening obstacles and as sites associated with dynamic strain aging.
Severe plastic deformation introduces a high density of dislocations and lattice defects.
Short, low-temperature annealing forms clusters that pin dislocations through Orowan strengthening without allowing substantial grain growth.
Dynamic strain aging or solute drag caused by the clusters will sustain strain hardening and delay premature necking.
The treated alloy will have more than 30% higher yield strength than the as-cast alloy.
The treated alloy will have more than 50% higher tensile elongation to failure than the as-cast alloy, with an illustrative change from below 5% to above 15%.

Solution annealing at approximately 1000 °C for one hour followed by water quenching typically produces a coarse-grained, single-phase microstructure with low dislocation density and limited strain hardening.
The strategy is applicable to MPEAs with moderate-to-high mixing enthalpy because solute clustering is thermodynamically favorable but kinetically hindered at low temperature.
In extremely high-melting-point systems, SPS may not provide enough diffusion for clustering during the proposed short treatment.
An annealing temperature that is too low will suppress clustering, whereas an excessively high temperature will permit grain growth and negate the proposed benefits.
